title: Packages and Advanced Java Syntax
goal: Packages, enums, records, sealed types, annotations aur generics ka first look.
objectives: Organise classes into packages and use imports correctly
Model fixed sets with enums and data carriers with records
Restrict a hierarchy with sealed interfaces
Read an annotation and explain what it does at compile or run time
definition: A package is a namespace and directory that groups related classes. Enums model a fixed set of constants. Records are compact immutable data carriers. Sealed types restrict which classes may implement or extend them. Annotations attach metadata that tools and frameworks read.
explain: Packages prevent name collisions and express ownership: com.brocode.shop.model, com.brocode.shop.service. The package statement must match the directory path, and import brings a type into scope without copying it.

An enum is a type with a fixed set of instances — perfect for statuses, roles and directions. A record declares its components once and generates a constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString. Both remove a large class of hand-written bugs.

A sealed interface names its permitted subtypes, so a switch over them can be exhaustive and the compiler knows the complete set. Annotations such as @Override, @FunctionalInterface and @Deprecated are checked by the compiler; framework annotations such as @Entity or @Service are read at runtime.
hinglish: Package namespace aur folder structure hai — com.brocode.shop.model jaise. Isse naam clash nahi hote aur ownership clear hoti hai. Enum fixed set of values ke liye, record immutable data carrier ke liye — dono boilerplate hataate hain.

Sealed interface batata hai kaun kaun implement kar sakta hai, isliye switch exhaustive ho sakta hai. Annotation metadata hai: @Override compiler check karta hai, @Entity jaisi annotations frameworks runtime par padhte hain.
analogy: Package ek building ka floor hai jahan related departments baithte hain; import intercom hai jisse doosre floor se baat karte ho. Record ek pre-printed form hai — fields ek baar bharo, baaki details system bhar deta hai.
why: Real Java projects are organised by package, and records/enums/sealed types are the modern way to model data precisely. Framework annotations are how Spring and JPA find your classes, so reading them is a daily skill.

syntax.note: A record's accessors are name() and price(), not getName(). The compact constructor validates before fields are assigned.
The enum switch expression is exhaustive without a default. A sealed interface limits who may implement it.

topics.title: Packages and imports
topics.body: package declares the namespace and must match the folder path. import brings one type (or a whole package with *) into scope; java.lang is imported automatically. Use fully qualified names when two packages share a class name.

topics.title: Access control across packages
topics.body: private is class-only, package-private (no modifier) is same-package, protected adds subclasses, public is everywhere. A public class must live in a file with the same name.

topics.title: Nested and anonymous classes
topics.body: A static nested class is a namespaced helper. An inner class keeps a link to its outer instance. An anonymous class implements an interface on the spot — still useful when a lambda cannot express state or multiple methods.

topics.title: Enums
topics.body: Enums are classes with a fixed set of instances; they can have fields, constructors and methods. values(), valueOf() and switch make them ideal for statuses. Compare with ==, which is safe for enum constants.

topics.title: Records
topics.body: record Point(int x, int y) generates a canonical constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString. Records are shallowly immutable and cannot extend a class. Add validation in a compact constructor.

topics.title: Sealed classes and interfaces
topics.body: sealed … permits Sub1, Sub2 restricts the hierarchy, which makes exhaustive switches possible and models closed domains such as payment results or shapes.

topics.title: Annotations and documentation
topics.body: @Override, @Deprecated, @SuppressWarnings and @FunctionalInterface are compile-time checks. Framework annotations configure runtime behaviour. Javadoc comments (/** … */) with @param and @return generate API documentation.

lines: The record declaration generates the constructor and accessors for all three components.
The compact constructor validates amount before the record is created.

The switch expression over the enum is exhaustive; the invalid order throws and is caught.

lines: The sealed interface permits exactly two record implementations.
circle area uses PI r²; the cast is safe because the hierarchy is closed.
Formatter is a static nested helper class, called through its class name.
Both areas are formatted to two decimals by the nested helper.

mistakes.why: Record accessors are named after the components, without a get prefix.
Enum constants are objects of the enum type, not Strings. Comparing to a String is always false, and == is the correct, null-safe comparison for enums.

debug.brief: This record is used with JavaBean accessors, so it does not compile. Fix the calls.
hints: Records generate accessors named after the components.
There is no getX() method on a record.

best: Organise by feature or layer, and keep package names lowercase.
Use records for immutable data transfer; do not add mutable state to them.
Use enums instead of String/int constants for fixed sets.
Seal a hierarchy when the set of subtypes is genuinely closed.
tip: If an interviewer asks 'record vs class', mention the generated members, immutability (shallow), the compact constructor, and that records cannot extend a class — then give a DTO or API-response use case.
revision: Packages are namespaces tied to directories; import brings types into scope.
Enums are fixed instance sets; compare with ==.
Records generate constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode, toString.
Sealed types restrict subtypes; annotations add checked metadata.

practice.title: Record inventory
practice.prompt: Create record Item(String name, int qty, double price) with validation and print its values.
practice.hint: Use a compact constructor to reject negative qty.

practice.title: Enum with fields
practice.prompt: Give enum Priority a level field and a label() method; print labels for all constants.

practice.title: Sealed result
practice.prompt: Model Success and Failure records implementing a sealed Result, then switch over them with instanceof checks.
practice.hint: Java 17 supports sealed types; use if/else instanceof for exhaustiveness without pattern switch.

mcqs.q: Which members does a record generate?
mcqs.explain: That is the record contract; accessors are named after the components.
sealed … permits restricts the hierarchy to the named subtypes.

mcqs.q: How should two enum constants be compared?
mcqs.explain: There is exactly one instance per constant, so == is correct and null-safe.

interview.q: When would you use a record instead of a normal class?
interview.a: For immutable data carriers where the state is the whole API: DTOs, API responses, value objects, composite map keys. Records remove boilerplate and make equality and printing correct by default. Use a class when you need mutable state, inheritance from a class, or behaviour that dominates the data.
interview.followUp: Are records deep-immutable? (No — components holding mutable objects are still mutable; copy defensively.)

interview.q: What problem do sealed classes solve?
interview.a: They let a library author declare the complete set of subtypes, so consumers and the compiler can reason exhaustively — switches become checkable and adding a subtype becomes a deliberate, visible change.
interview.followUp: How does that relate to pattern matching? (An exhaustive switch over a sealed hierarchy needs no default branch.)

lab.title: Day type with an enum
lab.brief: Read a day number 1-7. Print WEEKEND for 6 and 7, WEEKDAY for 1-5, INVALID otherwise. Use an enum and a switch expression.
hints: A switch expression over day can return the enum constant.

checkpoint.title: Modern Java syntax in place?
checks: I can write a validating record and use its accessors
I can switch over an enum exhaustively
I can explain what sealed permits and why it helps
